title: The Biggest AI Music Maker Wants to Label Its Own Songs
hook: Suno is adding watermarking and download rules to stem the flood of AI tracks clogging streaming services — a rare case of a generator volunteering to mark its output.
key_points: Suno announced watermarking technology plus a new download policy, per The Verge.
The stated goal: limit spammy AI tracks and make AI-generated music more transparent.
CEO Mikey Shulman laid out the principles in a blog post as the company seeks legitimacy.
A watermark is a hidden signal in the file identifying it as machine-generated.
Watermarks only work if they survive re-encoding — and only for tools that choose to add them.
content_html: Streaming services are drowning in machine-made tracks, and one of the companies most responsible is proposing to help. Suno announced watermarking technology and a revised download policy aimed at limiting spammy AI songs and making AI-generated music easier to identify, with CEO Mikey Shulman setting out the reasoning in a long blog post.
extra_html: A watermark here means a hidden signal baked into the audio file that marks it as machine-generated — not something you'd hear, but something a platform's software can check. The Verge reads the move as part of Suno's campaign for legitimacy with an industry that has mostly regarded it as a threat, and the incentives genuinely line up: a catalog buried under low-effort spam is worth less to everyone, Suno included. The limits are worth stating too. Watermarks are voluntary, so they cover only the generators that opt in; they can degrade or be stripped through re-encoding; and they identify the tool, not the intent. Useful infrastructure, then, rather than a solution — the honest platforms get better labeling, and anyone determined to pass AI work off as human still can.

related.title: Meta Built Its Own AI Watermark Instead of Using the Shared One
related.hook: Meta's new 'Content Seal' stamps an invisible mark on its AI images so they can be traced. The catch: Google already had a tool for that — and one shared standard works better than many.

related.title: Spotting AI-Made Content
related.hook: There are real tells for AI text and images — but they're fading fast, and 'AI detector' tools are unreliable. The durable skill is judging the source, not squinting at the pixels.

related.title: A Hack Exposed What an AI Music Generator Trained On
related.hook: Suno never said what music trained its AI. A hacking incident did the talking instead, reportedly exposing millions of songs and lyrics scraped from YouTube, Genius, and Deezer.

flashcards.prompt: What is a watermark on AI-generated media?
flashcards.back_html: A hidden signal embedded in the file that marks it as machine-generated, so platforms and tools can identify it later without relying on how it sounds or looks.

flashcards.prompt: What's the main limitation of watermarking as an anti-slop strategy?

choices.text: It only covers tools that voluntarily add marks, and marks can be stripped or degraded
It makes the audio quality noticeably worse
It only works on video, not audio

flashcards.explanation_html: A watermark is opt-in by the generator and vulnerable to re-encoding, so it helps with honest platforms and does little against someone determined to hide.

flashcards.prompt: Why would Suno want to label its own output?

choices.text: It's seeking legitimacy with the music industry while curbing spam that devalues its product
Regulators had already banned unlabeled AI music worldwide
Watermarks let it charge more per song

flashcards.explanation_html: The Verge frames the announcement as part of Suno's push for legitimacy — transparency and spam control serve its own long-term interests.
